correctness.rationale: The basepoint intersection of Fermat cubic G and circle H has 3 simple infinity points, two simple finite points at x+y=-2, and two double finite points (1,0),(0,1), totaling Bezout nine. Strict-transform gradients after first blowup at double points are independent, requiring exactly one further blowup each. Critical equations x(3x+2t)=y(3y+2t)=0 enumerate all finite singular members; Hessians show nodes. At t=-3/2 the first exceptional curves remain vertical bridges joining line and conic, creating I4 (not mere I2), with I2 at 3 and infinity and four I1 fibers. For the birational quartic w^2=(3s+2t)(4(1+t)-s^3-2ts^2), exact binary-quartic invariants I=16t^4 and J=16 B(t) yield 4I^3-J^2=6912D(t) and 4096t^12-1728D=64B^2, proving j formula and ramification at 0,1728,infinity. Independent sympy recomputed quartic identities and root coprimalities. Euler fibers sum 12. Rational surface rho=10; Shioda–Tate gives 10-2-(3+1+1)=3. Thus the all-complex geometric theorem is proved; no arithmetic MW rank or torsion assertions.
